rot.ideia.ex1.e1: At the start of the game, f7 is Black's weak point: only the king defends it.
rot.ideia.ex1.e2: Here, the queen on h5 and the bishop on c4 both aim at the same square: f7.
rot.ideia.ex1.e3: That is two attackers against one defender. The knight on f6 does not protect f7.
rot.ideia.ex1.p: Give checkmate with the queen, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.certo: That's right! Checkmate: it is the scholar's mate.
rot.ideia.ex1.revela: The queen captures on f7 with check. The bishop protects her: the king cannot capture her.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h5h7.1: The queen captures the pawn on h7, but nobody protects her there.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h5h7.2: The rook captures the queen: you lost 9 points for 1.
rot.ideia.ex1.err.h5h7.3: Let's go back: the right square is the one the bishop also aims at.
rot.ideia.ex1.fora: That move is not mate. Let's go back: look at the square the bishop aims at.
rot.ideia.ex1.volta: Give checkmate with the queen, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex1.l1: The black king is trapped by its own pieces: d8, e7 and f8 are taken or covered.
rot.ideia.ex1.l2: Remember the idea: queen and bishop together against f7, and the queen mates while protected.
rot.ideia.ex2.e1: Now one move earlier. The bishop on c4 already aims at f7, but alone it is not enough.
rot.ideia.ex2.e2: The queen is missing: she must reach a square from which she also aims at f7.
rot.ideia.ex2.p: Bring the queen to aim at f7, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.certo: That's right! From h5, the queen aims at f7 along the diagonal. She attacks e5 too.
rot.ideia.ex2.revela: The queen goes to h5: from there, she aims at f7 with the bishop. The threat is mate.
rot.ideia.ex2.alt.d1f3.1: That works too! From f3, the queen aims at f7 along the f-file.
rot.ideia.ex2.alt.d1f3.2: Look also at the queen on h5, the most common scholar's square.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1g4.1: On g4, the queen does not aim at f7. The bishop is still alone.
rot.ideia.ex2.err.d1g4.2: Let's go back: look for a square from which the queen sees f7.
rot.ideia.ex2.fora: From that square, the queen does not aim at f7. Let's go back to the position.
rot.ideia.ex2.volta: Bring the queen to aim at f7, or click {verResposta}
rot.ideia.ex2.l1: Black does not see the threat and brings out the knight.
rot.ideia.ex2.l2: The knight on f6 attacks the queen, but does not protect f7. The mate is ready.
rot.ideia.ex2.l3: Remember the idea: first the bishop, then the queen, both against f7.
rot.ideia.ex2.l4: Now I will show the whole scholar's mate and a teacher's warning.
rot.demos.pastor.e1: The scholar's mate from start to finish. White opens the way for the bishop and the queen.
rot.demos.pastor.l1: The king's pawn moves two squares: the bishop and the queen get a path.
rot.demos.pastor.l3: The bishop goes to c4 and already aims at f7.
rot.demos.pastor.l5: The queen goes to h5: now it is two against f7.
rot.demos.pastor.l6: Black attacks the queen and forgets f7.
rot.demos.pastor.l7: The queen captures on f7: checkmate in four moves.
rot.demos.aviso.e1: A teacher's warning: bringing the queen out early has a price.
rot.demos.aviso.l1: White aims at f7 with the bishop. The threat is mate.
rot.demos.aviso.l2: But Black defends and also attacks the queen.
rot.demos.aviso.l3: The queen has to run. She aims at f7 again, now from f3.
rot.demos.aviso.l4: The knight blocks the way and comes into play. The queen has already made three moves.
rot.demos.aviso.l5: Against someone who defends well, the queen becomes a target. Use the trick, but develop your pieces.
rot.demos.aviso.l6: Now it's your turn: give the scholar's mate.
rot.pratica.inteiro.enunciado: Give the scholar's mate: king's pawn, bishop to c4, queen to h5 and mate on f7.
rot.pratica.inteiro.fim: Well done. Four moves, and the scholar's mate is done.
rot.pratica.deF3.enunciado: Now the queen is on f3. Give checkmate.
rot.pratica.deF3.fim: Perfect. From h5 or from f3, the target is always f7.
